import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    if len(feats.ids) == 0:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Check for correlation-based near-duplicates
    corr_pairs = []
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                corr_pairs.append((feats.ids[i], feats.ids[j]))
    
    # Build set of unique features (remove near-duplicates once)
    unique_ids = set(feats.ids)
    for a, b in corr_pairs:
        if a in unique_ids and b in unique_ids:
            # Remove one of the pair (prefer higher effect size)
            # For simplicity, remove the second one
            unique_ids.remove(b)
    
    # Compute effect sizes using Welch's t-test
    effects = {}
    for fid in unique_ids:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col_idx]
        y = feats.y
        group0 = x[y==0]
        group1 = x[y==1]
        if len(group0) > 0 and len(group1) > 0:
            t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1, equal_var=False)
            effects[fid] = abs(t_stat)
        else:
            effects[fid] = 0
    
    # Sort by effect size
    sorted_effects = sorted(effects.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # Check if any effect is significant (p < 0.05)
    # Use simple logistic regression to test significance within strata
    drivers = []
    columns = []
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    
    # Try to find drivers by checking stratum-wise association
    strata = list(set(feats.stratum))
    if len(strata) == 1:
        # No stratification, just use all features
        candidates = [fid for fid, eff in sorted_effects[:10]]  # Top 10
        for fid in candidates:
            col_idx = feats.column(fid)
            x = feats.x[:, col_idx]
            model = LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=True, max_iter=1000)
            model.fit(x.reshape(-1,1), feats.y)
            if abs(model.coef_[0][0]) > 0.1:  # arbitrary threshold
                drivers.append(fid)
                columns.append(fid)
                loadings[fid] = model.coef_[0][0]
                if len(drivers) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
                    break
    else:
        # Stratified analysis
        stratum_results = defaultdict(list)
        for stratum in strata:
            mask = np.array(feats.stratum) == stratum
            stratum_x = feats.x[mask]
            stratum_y = feats.y[mask]
            
            for fid in unique_ids:
                col_idx = feats.column(fid)
                x = stratum_x[:, col_idx]
                if np.std(x) > 1e-10:  # avoid constant features
                    model = LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=True, max_iter=1000)
                    try:
                        model.fit(x.reshape(-1,1), stratum_y)
                        stratum_results[fid].append(model.coef_[0][0])
                    except:
                        pass
        
        # Take features with consistent effects across strata
        for fid in unique_ids:
            coefs = stratum_results.get(fid, [])
            if len(coefs) >= len(strata)/2 and np.std(coefs) < 0.5:  # consistency check
                # Add to drivers if strong effect
                if effects[fid] > 2.0:  # threshold for being "mechanistic"
                    drivers.append(fid)
                    columns.append(fid)
                    loadings[fid] = np.mean(coefs)
                    if len(drivers) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
                        break
    
    # Ensure we don't exceed MAX_DRIVERS
    if len(drivers) > MAX_DRIVERS:
        drivers = drivers[:MAX_DRIVERS]
        columns = columns[:MAX_DRIVERS]
        # Trim loadings to match
        loadings = {k: v for i, (k, v) in enumerate(loadings.items()) if i < MAX_DRIVERS}
    
    # If no strong drivers found, return empty
    if not drivers:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Return final design
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(drivers),
        columns=tuple(columns),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
